newsitem.title: FRANCE: French chemist investigated over deadly hormones.
newsitem.headline: French chemist investigated over deadly hormones.

text.p: A magistrate has launched an inquiry into whether a French official knowingly distributed tainted growth hormones blamed for killing 40 children in France, judicial sources said on Wednesday.

Marc Mollet, a former senior official at the state-run Central Hospitals' Pharmacy, was placed under investigation for possible poisoning on Tuesday over the distribution of about 20,000 doses of the hormone, outlawed from June 1985, they said.

Magistrate Marie-Odile Bertella-Geffroy is already investiagting four other people for manslaughter in the case, in which children suffering from dwarfism were treated with tainted hormones from 1984-86.
"Poisoning" is a more serious charge than manslaughter and can bring a 30-year jail sentence.

After the June 1985 ban, investigators suspect that old stocks of the hormone, extracted from the pituitary glands of corpses, were used up to save money even though officials were aware the hormones risked causing Creutzfeldt-Jakob (CJD) disease.
A variant of CJD is the human equivalent of mad cow disease.
About 50 children treated with the hormone from 1984-86 contracted CJD after being treated with the contaminated products, and 40 of them have since died, lawyers for the victims say.

"In the whole world there are only 90 victims and 50 French people among them. The action of the French health authorities in this matter has been disastrous," said lawyer Monique Pelletier. "This is a sad record held by France."
The state-run Central Hospital Pharmacy distributes medicines to hospitals.
The case has similarities to the distribution of AIDS-tainted blood products in France in the 1980s. More than 1,250 haemophiliacs were infected and more than 400 have since died.
